title: Recurring dreams and daydreams of five empty worlds (and one non-empty)
content: This is my first post in this community, since I've just learned about it today. Since around 2020 I've been obsessed with a particular experience I had, and searched for others with similar experiences. The Mallworld concept is the closest thing I've ever seen to describing my experiences. I've been writing a document for years (84 pages loong now) detailing anything I've seen others talking about that seemed similar, talking about media that seemed related, psychological theories for why these experiences occurred, and so on. I'll describe my experiences in the hopes that others have seen the same places. I'm withholding some details merely for brevity and to avoid explaining every intricacy I've seen so far. The first world consists of an infinite city in permanent night, which is artificially lit by neon signs and the lights from inside buildings and streetlights - all the typical artificial light sources in a city, essentially. No one else is present, not even animals. Regardless of that fact, storefronts are unlocked and seemingly "open," even restaurants. If I enter a restaurant with a particular food in mind, or a store with a particular item in mind that the type of store might reasonably have, I'll always find it (and in the case of the restaurant, it will be as though it were just prepared and left for me, like a pickup order). I have a particular house in a high-rise that I stay in. The second world consists of an infinite suburb in the desert, where it is always daytime. This location is definitely based on an actual place I lived, so the explanation for its appearance is fairly mundane. Like the city, no one is present. In this location, the place I am staying at functions like the storefronts do in the city, but on a smaller scale - things appear when I need them, so long as they might reasonably be found in a certain room. (For example, food will appear in the kitchen if I enter that room while looking to eat, but not in the living room.) There are also stores which function like those in the city, but much further away. Locations move around in this location, seemingly based on convenience - if I walk to a location in the city, it takes just as long to walk back from it, but if I walk to a location in this dream-suburb, the time it takes to walk back is halved, or even quartered. The third and fourth worlds consist respectively of infinite roads on which I'm driving, and of a train riding though an infinite, misty forest. In both locations, it is either dawn or dusk, but the sun never rises or sets any further. Once again, there are no people, no other cars, etc. In the road-world, I never exit the car, and feel no real need to eat or drink. In the train-world, I typically don't feel the need to eat, but if I do, one of the train-cars functions similarly to the storefronts in the city-world or the kitchen in the suburb-world. The fifth world is accessible from parks in the city-world, but impossibly leads to another infinite location where it is also always night, but also always snowing. This location is an infinite place of snowy hills, where the snow is fixed around 3-4 inches deep everywhere. There are single houses spread apart by long distances, which are never visible from one another. Unlike other dream-locations I've discussed so far, I both feel the need to eat and drink in this world, and there is no guaranteed source of food. There is hunting equipment in some of the hosues and, unlike the other worlds, there are animals, though they are still rare - these are mostly deer and bears. There is at least one Christmas village that exists in the place of a house in a valley between the hills, which is lit with Christmas lights and displays, but likewise has no people, and the animals don't approach it. The sixth and final world is the only one which is neither empty of creatures nor sparsely populated. This world is again one with permanent night, but the sky glows unnaturally, making the world more visible than it normally would be. This world is filled with dangerous creatures of many varities, resembling things found in horror stories. I've kept a catalogue of the particular types I've seen, but there seem to be only around a dozen common types. This world is hellish and dangerous, and this is visible in the landscape itself, with carrion being strewn about in many locations, and some balconies appearing to be stained with overflowing blood. If any of these locations seem familiar, I'd love to hear from you! I've been trying to figure out what these recurring locations mean for years.
